record.paper_title: Combinatorial properties of continuous graphs: A survey of challenges, solutions and open problems
record.original_question: For a continuous graph Γ, let χ_{1/2}(Γ) be its radius-1/2 chromatic number. Does the strong inapproximability known for the ordinary chromatic number of combinatorial graphs also hold for χ_{1/2}(Γ) on continuous graphs? More concretely, does the same kind of hardness of approximation persist in the continuous setting?

evidence.quote: The question for the continuous version of the chromatic number problem remains as above: Whether or not the same hardness of approximation remains for the 1/2-chromatic number problem on continuous graphs?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let (V, d) be a (separable) metric space, and let Γ = (V, E) be a continuous graph, meaning that V is equipped with a Borel measurable structure and E ⊆ V × V is a symmetric Borel subset (no loops). For r > 0, define the radius-r chromatic number χ_r(Γ) as the smallest cardinality (or measurable cardinality) of a partition V = ⋃_i C_i into Borel "color classes" C_i such that for every i and every pair of distinct points x, y ∈ C_i one has d(x, y) > r and (x, y) ∉ E. In particular χ_{1/2}(Γ) is the radius-1/2 chromatic number.

It is known that for ordinary finite graphs G on n vertices, for every ε > 0 it is NP-hard to approximate the chromatic number χ(G) within a factor n^{1−ε}.

Question: Does an analogous strong inapproximability result hold for χ_{1/2}(Γ) in the setting of continuous graphs? Concretely, prove or disprove that the radius-1/2 chromatic number of a continuous graph is hard to approximate within a comparable factor (e.g., that no efficient algorithm can approximate χ_{1/2}(Γ) within any sub-polynomial factor of an appropriate size parameter of Γ, unless a standard complexity assumption fails).
artifact.category_tag: Hardness of approximation for chromatic numbers on continuous graphs
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search returned only classical hardness-of-approximation results for the ordinary chromatic number on finite graphs (e.g., Zuckerman's n^{1−ε} hardness, Huang's improved bounds for K-colorable graphs). No results addressing the radius-1/2 chromatic number on continuous graphs were found, and the question is explicitly posed as open in the surveying source. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: Improved Hardness of Approximating Chromatic Number
status_evidence.snippet: For sufficiently large K, it is NP-hard to color K-colorable graphs with less than 2^Ω(K^{1/3}) colors.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art hardness for chromatic number is in the discrete/finite setting; no analog stated for continuous graphs.

status_evidence.title: On the Hardness of Approximating the Chromatic Number
status_evidence.snippet: Unless NP=ZPP, no polynomial-time algorithm approximates the chromatic number of χ-colorable graphs within χ^{1/5 − o(1)}.
status_evidence.claim: Strong inapproximability results known only for combinatorial graphs.
